discipline: philosophy (Heideggerian phenomenology; comparative literary-philosophical critique; ideology-critique of Heidegger's Rektoratszeit)
thesis: Heidegger's FCM boredom lecture (1929/30) reads profound boredom's disclosive 'message' in a way that is never ideologically neutral: the third form's insight into meaninglessness is immediately re-absorbed into an activist demand for resolute, work-defined self-assertion that directly foreshadows Heidegger's 1933/34 Rektoratszeit collaboration with the NSDAP Arbeitsstaat; Fernando Pessoa's Book of Disquiet, read as a sustained refusal of that demand, supplies a non-activist counter-model of dwelling affirmatively within depersonalized, meaningless detachment, and stands as the paper's own 'antidote to philosophy.'

sections.title: 1. Introduction: An antidote to philosophy
sections.summary: Frames the Book of Disquiet as a deliberate counter-image to philosophy's confident, epistemically sovereign voice; states the anti-'activist' thesis via Adorno's aphorism that philosophy is 'the most serious matter' yet 'not all that serious'; previews that Pessoa will 'come out on top' against Heidegger.

sections.title: 2. Boredom and Resolute Being in Heidegger
sections.summary: Reconstructs FCM's basic framing (boredom as Grundstimmung that 'sleeps' until awakened); brackets the first form; gives a close reading of the second form (full German dinner-party quotation) and third form (undifferentiated no one, telling refusal, disclosive message, Augenblick); argues Heidegger's construal of the message as a demand for resolute action is an unargued activist imposition, evidenced by the lecture's turn 'from about section 38 onward' toward proto-Nazi rhetoric.

sections.title: 3. Interlude: The collapse of dasein and work in the Rektoratszeit
sections.summary: Via Werner Hamacher's critique of Heidegger's Rektorats-Philosophie, traces how 'work' (Arbeit) comes, in the 1933 speech to the unemployed and the 1934 Logic Lecture, to occupy the structural place FCM/Being and Time reserve for the Augenblick; notes postwar German continuity in prizing Arbeit despite repudiating Nazism generally; closes by calling for 'the antidote.'

sections.title: 4. Pessoa, or the Ecstasy of Not-Being
sections.summary: Introduces Bernardo Soares and Pessoa's heteronyms via a Badiou epigraph; reads the Book of Disquiet in three self-declared stages (factlessness/non-existence, p.249-250; tentative self-fashioned passivity and writing-as-sanctuary, p.250-253; literature as 'the art of making real,' p.253-256); compares and contrasts Pessoa's 'perishing' with Heidegger's Being and Time account of authentic dying; closes with the 'shepherds of being' generalization about literature as philosophy's corrective.

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: central construct; undifferentiated no one, total indifference of beings as a whole, disclosive 'message,' call to the Augenblick

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: full German block quotation + own paraphrase; standing now (stehendes Jetzt); self-formed, abandoned span of lifetime

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: named only via the train-station example; explicitly bracketed 'in order to have more space for the two deeper manifestations'

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: connective construct; Langeweile as lived-time-becoming-long; profound boredom as fusion of past/present/future into a stretched horizon

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: third-form total indifference ('melody of duration has ceased'); paralleled later by Pessoa's 'complete and absolute tedium'

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: reconstructed via the disclosive 'message' faithfully, then contested as over-extended once Heidegger reads it as demanding resolute action

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: two registers: dinner-party surface engagement masking underlying boredom; later, Pessoa's non-instrumental aesthetic absorption in writing as a non-activist alternative

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: loosely present via Pessoa's torpor/slumber fragments ('drunk on not being'); literary register, not a cognitive-science construct

readings.claim: The FCM boredom lecture is performative, not merely descriptive: it aims to awaken in the listener/reader the very attunement it describes.
The second form's emptiness is self-formed: a freely chosen, outwardly agreeable evening becomes, in retrospect, a lost and self-abandoned span of lifetime.
The third form dissolves the bounded 'span' of the second form into an indefinitely stretched horizon in which all beings, self included, become uniformly indifferent.
Heidegger's reading is not neutral: its tone betrays 'the nervous unrest of the activist,' and the insight into meaninglessness is immediately re-absorbed into a mobilizing call to arms.

This activist re-absorption is continuous with Heidegger's later trajectory: the 1933 'Rede an Arbeitslose' and 1934 Logic Lecture install Arbeit at exactly the structural place FCM/BT reserve for the Augenblick.
Heidegger's text forecloses, without argument, the possibility that lingering in profound boredom might harbor its own bliss or peace of mind rather than demanding resolute action.

Pessoa's Book of Disquiet answers this foreclosed question affirmatively through literary practice: settling into tedium as a wellspring for poetic production rather than breaking its spell through resolute action.

Pessoa's narrator merely 'perishes' rather than dying existentially, paralleling but failing to qualify for Heidegger's Being and Time account of authentic death, since a life without resolute care lacks the required existential ending.
Despite the sharp contrast, literature itself becomes Pessoa's own existential commitment, so the two authors are 'not all that far apart' in this one respect.
Novelists and poets, Pessoa above all, are 'the true shepherds of being,' offering philosophy a needed corrective to its own over-assured, unitary construals of the subject.

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
interlocutors.role: primary phenomenological source and primary target of the paper's ideology-critique

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — Being and Time
interlocutors.role: background for the Augenblick (§65 cross-reference, Slaby p.242 n.15) and the account of authentic death used contrastively against Pessoa

interlocutors.name: Pessoa, Fernando (Bernardo Soares / Book of Disquiet)
interlocutors.role: central literary counter-interlocutor; supplies the non-activist alternative to Heidegger's resolute existence

interlocutors.name: Badiou, Alain
interlocutors.role: cited for the heteronymy-as-'dispositif for thinking' reading of Pessoa; explicitly distinguished from Slaby's own narrower, deconstructive-of-philosophical-subjectivity reading

interlocutors.name: Hamacher, Werner
interlocutors.role: source of the Rektorats-Philosophie critique and the Arbeit/Augenblick displacement thesis

interlocutors.name: Hörl, Erich
interlocutors.role: cited as extending Hamacher's technology-focused reworking of the Arbeit thesis

interlocutors.name: Haugeland, John
interlocutors.role: cited (Dasein Disclosed) for the standard English scholarly uptake of 'dasein'

interlocutors.name: Adorno, Theodor W.
interlocutors.role: epigraph aphorism framing the anti-activist thesis

interlocutors.name: Ahmed, Sara
interlocutors.role: Willful Subjects footnoted alongside a reflexive caveat that the Heidegger/Pessoa contrast is staged between two privileged white male authors

tensions.axis: boredom's disclosure as demanding resolute self-assertive action (Heidegger) vs. boredom's disclosure as licensing affirmed, undemanding dwelling in depersonalized detachment (Pessoa)
tensions.note: The paper's central staged opposition; deliberately weighted toward Pessoa from the introduction onward, not resolved as a genuine toss-up.

tensions.axis: profound boredom's exegesis as textually necessitated vs. profound boredom's exegesis as ideologically imported activism
tensions.note: Slaby's polemical claim that Heidegger's own construal is not required by the phenomenon itself but reflects (and later feeds) Heidegger's political-existential temperament.

tensions.axis: high-fidelity restatement of FCM's three forms vs. explicit political-historical contestation
tensions.note: The paper shifts register partway through §2, mirroring the same restatement-to-contestation pattern this cluster observes in bor-sec-13 (2010) — a cross-paper structural echo, not a claim either paper makes about itself (P/anticipatory-application).
